searchText: > A comes in slot N before the deadline, B comes later, after the deadline in slot N. from whose point of view? different validators may see A and B in different orders and on different sides of the deadline - so how to determine which of the 2 is the correct one and which is the malicious one? are you expecting builders to have released payloads in this situation? > from whose point of view? From the majority of the chain, each individual attester will act according to their own timestamps. > are you expecting builders to have released payloads in this situation? I don't, but I want builders to be protected **even** in the scenario in which the block A is both a) not weak and b) not head, because builders may have broadcast the payload and they are protected by the forkchoice rules (eg. Builders may not have seen the equivocating block at all). FWIW, builders should be aware of the nuances of forkchoice here, if A is not weak then A will actually be boosted and the next proposer will have to propose on top of it, the builder is safe to broadcast with as little as 20% of the attestations for it. However, builders would only be charged if they don't broadcast when A is not only not weak but actually strong, that is, it reaches 60% of the vote.

FWIW, builders should be aware of the nuances of forkchoice here, if A is not weak then A will actually be boosted and the next proposer will have to propose on top of it, the builder is safe to broadcast with as little as 20% of the attestations for it. However, builders would only be charged if they don't broadcast when A is not only not weak but actually strong, that is, it reaches 60% of the vote.
